PHYSICS — TERMLY EXAM #2
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: PHYSICS
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. Movement of water only across a membrane
   D. Heating until a solid melts

2. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. Any substance that conducts electricity
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

3. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Milk souring
   C. Iron rusting
   D. Ice melting to water

4. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 100 °C
   B. 0 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 50 °C

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Introduction to Physics? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Physics.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Introduction to Physics.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Introduction to Physics.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Introduction to Physics.

6. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

7. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Primary consumers only
   B. Producers
   C. Tertiary consumers
   D. Decomposers only

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Energy, Work, Power and Machines? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Energy, Work, Power and Machines.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Energy, Work, Power and Machines.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Energy, Work, Power and Machines.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Energy, Work, Power and Machines.

9. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Overgrazing continuously
   B. Removing all vegetation
   C. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   D. Burning crop residue every week

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Greenhouse Effect and Climate Change? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Greenhouse Effect and Climate Change.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Greenhouse Effect and Climate Change.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Greenhouse Effect and Climate Change.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Greenhouse Effect and Climate Change.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Pressure? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Pressure.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Pressure.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Pressure.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Pressure.

13. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. watt (W)
   B. joule (J)
   C. newton (N)
   D. pascal (Pa)

14. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Properties of Waves? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Properties of Waves.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Properties of Waves.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Properties of Waves.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Properties of Waves.

15. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Mechanical Properties of Materials? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Mechanical Properties of Materials.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Mechanical Properties of Materials.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Mechanical Properties of Materials.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Mechanical Properties of Materials.

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Temperature and Thermal Expansion? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Temperature and Thermal Expansion.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Temperature and Thermal Expansion.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Temperature and Thermal Expansion.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Temperature and Thermal Expansion.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Greenhouse Effect and Climate Change 4.2 Introduction to Space Physics Page 15 o and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Greenhouse Effect and Climate Change and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Introduction to Space Physics Page 15 of 62 1 STRAND 1.0 MECHANICS AND THERMAL P and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Introduction to Space Physics and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Introduction to Physics and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Pressure and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
